executive_summary: The House voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to send impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth back to committee, halting the effort until Democrats take the majority in January; a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday found 71 percent of Americans want Congress to pass legislation ending the conflict with Iran. The read is that the Iran campaign now runs on a legislative clock rather than a military one, with Democrats having vowed to act when they take power on January 3, and I would be wrong if Trumps claim at Arlington that the war would be over soon is borne out before any vote. Watch SpaceXs 15th Starship flight, with a window of 5:45 to 7 p.m. ET on Friday, November 13 and a planned catch of the returning upper stage at Starbase: a successful recovery supports the case for cadence before any move to Kennedy Space Center, while a loss pushes that transition out.
opportunity_of_the_day: Kratos has signed a long-term agreement with Seagate Space for the first Gateway offshore launch platform, targeting a first mission in 2027, as Seagate Space executed its first platform construction contract. What this means is that offshore launch has moved into build, and the trade works only if construction milestones hold.
risk_of_the_day: British police arrested a 41-year-old US soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, a day after US refuelling aircraft were removed from a British airbase, which the Wall Street Journal attributed to a threat from Iran. The read is that allied basing in Britain is the near-term fragility, and it moves fast.

space.signal: SpaceX is preparing its 15th Starship flight with a window of 5:45 to 7 p.m. ET on Friday, November 13, targeting recovery of the returning upper stage at Starbase after a planned 22-hour mission of as many as 14 orbits.
space.watch: Starship flight 15 upper stage catch at Starbase
space.bull: A successful catch at the launch site validates the recovery concept and supports the cadence case for operators booking rides, alongside Rocket Labs ESCAPADE spacecraft completing powered Earth flybys toward Mars, with RKLB up 5.49 percent at the last close.
space.bear: A loss of the upper stage or a scrubbed window delays the Starbase-to-Kennedy Space Center transition and leaves launch customers more dependent on existing vehicles for longer.

defence.signal: Democrats, who won their largest congressional majorities since at least 2008 in last weeks midterms, have vowed to act on the Iran war and tariff repeal when they take power on January 3, after the House sent the Hegseth impeachment articles back to committee by 211 to 204.
defence.watch: Democratic majority seated January 3 and Iran war legislation
defence.bull: If procurement momentum holds regardless of the political fight, European air defence demand of the kind Belgium showed with its NASAMS, 20 Rheinmetall Skyranger 30 systems and Thales GM200 MM/C radars carries the sector, as does the fiscal 2027 Collaborative Combat Aircraft request of $2.37 billion.
defence.bear: Legislation ending the conflict with Iran, backed by 71 percent of Americans in the Reuters/Ipsos poll, would compress consumption-driven demand and put the burden on multi-year programme orders rather than operations.

geo.signal: G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris on November 9 and 10 condemned Irans disruption of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and called on Tehran to resume full cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency, while Saudi Arabia said it intercepted three cruise missiles towards Riyadh and drones aimed at Mecca.
geo.watch: Hormuz shipping attacks and Iran cooperation with the IAEA
geo.bull: No date is given for either, so this is a standing indicator: fewer attacks on civilian vessels and a resumption of IAEA cooperation would ease the regional risk premium and shift attention back to scheduled procurement.
geo.bear: Continued Hormuz disruption and further Houthi strikes, against a World Health Organisation count of more than 320,000 displaced in Yemen since August 1 and 11,755 casualties as of November 8, keep shipping and force protection costs elevated.

stocks.notable_movers: At its last close RKLB led all names with a gain of 5.49 percent, while ASTS advanced 8.70 percent, both outpacing the defence primes and signalling that new-space and satellite connectivity names drew buying interest in the most recent session. Among the primes LMT at $610.05 added 1.15 percent and RTX at $201.29 gained 0.51 percent, modest moves that reflect cautious positioning rather than conviction ahead of fast-moving Iran war political developments.
stocks.sector_outlook: European air defence procurement is accelerating structurally, with Belgiums NOK 10 billion ($1 billion) NASAMS order the latest signal that NATO eastern-flank anxiety is driving multi-year platform spending that benefits Kongsberg, Rheinmetall and Thales through the decade.

stories.headline: Starship flight 15 targets upper stage catch at Starbase
stories.context: SpaceX is preparing its 15th Starship test flight from Starbase in Texas, targeting the recovery of the returning upper stage back at the launch site, with a launch window opening from 5:45 to 7 p.m. ET on Friday, November 13. Ship 42 is planned to circle Earth as many as 14 times during a 22-hour mission before attempting to return to Starbase. The mission follows Starships orbital flight at the end of September and is widely regarded as a potential final Texas launch before a debut at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
stories.implication: A successful upper-stage catch would validate full reusability of the worlds most capable heavy-lift vehicle and materially accelerate the cadence at which SpaceX can compete for government and commercial payload contracts requiring very large mass-to-orbit.

stories.headline: ESCAPADE smallsats head to Mars after powered Earth flybys
stories.context: NASAs two ESCAPADE spacecraft, Blue and Gold, completed powered flybys of Earth roughly 48 hours apart, using the Oberth effect to propel themselves toward Mars in what NASA describes as the first time a NASA spacecraft used a powered Earth flyby to reach Mars. Gold flew by Earth at about 6 a.m. Eastern on November 9, coming within about 1,050 kilometers, while Blue made a similar flyby at an altitude of about 1,600 kilometers. The Rocket Lab-built spacecraft had loitered near the Earth-sun L-2 Lagrange point for nearly a year after launching on Blue Origins New Glenn last November.
stories.implication: The mission demonstrates that non-traditional Mars trajectories using powered flybys can open launch windows beyond the standard two-year cycle, reducing mission planning constraints for future NASA and commercial deep-space programmes.

stories.headline: US Air Force CCAs fly multi-ship formation for first time
stories.context: The US Air Force flew multiple Collaborative Combat Aircraft in formation and executed beyond-visual-range counter-air tactics on October 26, using Shields Hivemind autonomy software in what the company describes as the first multi-ship CCA flight demonstration. The Air Force has stated an intent to field 500 combat-ready semi-autonomous systems by 2032, with an overall fleet size of 1,000. The fiscal 2027 budget request included 996.5 million dollars in procurement funding alongside 150 million dollars in advanced procurement and 1.37 billion dollars in continued research and development, for a total program request of 2.37 billion dollars.
stories.implication: The milestone accelerates the credibility timeline for semi-autonomous combat aircraft, sharpening competition between CCA programme participants and increasing the near-term relevance of autonomy software providers such as Shield.

stories.headline: Senate panel to vote on NASA CFO and inspector general nominees
stories.context: The Senate Commerce Committee held a hearing on November 10 to consider nominations for Joshua Shoemaker as NASAs chief financial officer and Robert Steinau as inspector general, two of the four Senate-confirmed positions at the agency. Neither nominee drew significant questioning, with senators focusing primarily on the concurrent nomination of Danielle Thumann to the Federal Communications Commission. The Senate Commerce Committee announced on November 11 that it will meet November 18 to vote on the nominees, sending them, if approved, to the full Senate for a confirmation vote.
stories.implication: Filling NASAs top financial oversight roles matters for defence-adjacent space investors because programme budget transparency and audit accountability directly affect congressional willingness to sustain large-platform spending such as the Space Launch System into the 2030s.

stories.headline: Kratos signs long-term deal for Seagate Space offshore platform
stories.context: Kratos Defense and Security Solutions has signed a long-term agreement with Seagate Space for use of the companys first Gateway offshore launch platform, targeting a first mission from the platform in 2027 with multiple additional launches anticipated in each subsequent year. The announcement coincides with Seagate Space executing its first Gateway platform construction contract, moving the mobile offshore launch concept from planning into physical build. Kratos plans to use the Gateway platform initially in support of defense-related launch and target missions.
stories.implication: Mobile offshore launch capability adds resilience and geographic flexibility to US national security launch options, reducing dependence on fixed ranges that are increasingly regarded as single points of failure in a contested-access environment.

stories.headline: House blocks Hegseth impeachment in 211 to 204 vote
stories.context: The House voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to send impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth back to committee, effectively halting the effort until Democrats take the majority in January. Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky led the eight-count resolution, which focused largely on the war in Iran but also referenced military actions in Yemen and Venezuela. Hegseth held his first news conference at the Pentagon in six months to rebuff the effort, calling the charges policy disagreements and not impeachable offenses.
stories.implication: The delay rather than defeat of impeachment leaves a sword over the Pentagon leadership through the transition, complicating long-cycle procurement decisions and creating uncertainty for contractors dependent on stable civilian oversight.

stories.headline: 71 percent of Americans want Congress to end Iran war
stories.context: A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday found 71 percent of Americans, including 93 percent of Democrats and 51 percent of Republicans, want Congress to pass legislation ending the conflict with Iran that Trump launched alongside Israel in February. A smaller but still significant share of respondents, 62 percent, said they would support an effort to repeal tariffs on imports put in place by the Trump administration. Democrats, who won their largest congressional majorities since at least 2008 in last weeks midterms, have vowed to act on the Iran war and tariff repeal when they take power on January 3.
stories.implication: A legislative end to the Iran war before or shortly after January 3 would abruptly shift US defence spending priorities away from active-campaign sustainment toward readiness recapitalisation, with direct implications for munitions makers, logistics contractors and energy-exposed sectors.

stories.headline: Belgium orders NASAMS, Skyranger 30 and GM200 for air defence
stories.context: Belgium has ordered major elements for its Blue Dome air defence system, including Kongsberg National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System medium-range air defence, 20 Rheinmetall Skyranger 30 short-range air defence systems and Thales GM200 MM/C radars. The NASAMS order, worth 10 billion Norwegian kroner, was marked by a formal ceremony on November 9, while Thales announced a contract of undisclosed amount and number for GM200 MM/Cs on November 10. Belgium is described as the 18th country to select NASAMS, with the deal being fulfilled through the Netherlands.
stories.implication: Belgiums commitment deepens the multinational NASAMS production base, supporting higher-volume manufacturing economies and reinforcing Kongsberg as a structural beneficiary of European air defence re-arming.

stories.headline: Russia-linked hackers stole NATO and EU emails from Romania
stories.context: Slovak cybersecurity firm ESET revealed on November 10 that the Turla hacking group, assessed as affiliated with Russias FSB, compromised Romanian government Microsoft Exchange servers in December 2025, using a tool suite dubbed Cereal to scan for and copy emails referencing NATO and EU addresses. ESET first detected the Cereal toolset being used against a Kazakh government agency in November 2025 before discovering the Romanian intrusion roughly a month later. ESET attributed the toolset to Turla with high confidence, citing the simultaneous use of another component publicly linked to the group and conceptual similarities to older Turla malware.
stories.implication: Persistent FSB targeting of NATO-adjacent government email infrastructure signals that signals intelligence collection against alliance coordination is active and ongoing, raising the operational security burden for any country managing shared intelligence through standard email platforms.

stories.headline: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of Russia espionage
stories.context: British police arrested a 41-year-old senior US soldier near the city of Gloucester, west England, on Tuesday on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, with FBI Director Kash Patel describing the case as involving allegations of espionage of the utmost concern to the United States and its allies. The arrest followed by one day the removal of US refuelling aircraft from a British airbase, which the Wall Street Journal attributed to a threat from Iran. The US had also withdrawn bombers from RAF Fairford in September over a separate incident police have linked to Iran.
stories.implication: Simultaneous insider-threat and external Iran-linked security incidents at UK-based US assets signal a compounding vulnerability posture for trans-Atlantic basing arrangements that operators and planners must weigh against forward deployment assumptions.

stories.headline: Houthis deny targeting Mecca as Yemen fighting surges
stories.context: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted three cruise missiles launched towards Riyadh and drones aimed at Mecca and southern regions, with Saudi civil defence reporting debris from two intercepted ballistic missiles falling in the village of Sabuhah in Mecca province. A Houthi spokesperson rejected what he called Saudi lies, saying the group targeted a pumping station in Yanbu and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport instead. The World Health Organisation reported more than 320,000 people displaced in Yemen since August 1 and casualties rising sharply to 11,755, including 2,098 killed and 9,657 wounded, as of November 8.
stories.implication: Disputed targeting of Mecca raises the political stakes sharply and increases pressure on Saudi Arabia and the GCC to accelerate air and missile defence procurement and integration.

stories.headline: Trump claims US did not start war with Iran
stories.context: US President Donald Trump, speaking at the national Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery, claimed that Iran had been waging war on America since 1979 and that his administration fought back and won, adding that the war would be over soon without giving a clear date. Trump said he began operations against Iran seven months ago, described only a few weeks of active hard fighting, and said the US lost 18 service members. Trump added that it would take Iran 25 years to rebuild what has been destroyed.
stories.implication: Trumps framing of a near-complete victory sits in tension with ongoing operations and pending Democratic congressional pressure to end the conflict, creating uncertainty over the duration and scope of US regional military commitments that directly affects Gulf defence posture planning.

stories.headline: G7 condemns Iran Hormuz disruption, backs Ukraine
stories.context: G7 foreign ministers, meeting in Paris on November 9 and 10, condemned Irans disruption of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, calling on Tehran to cease attacks against civilian vessels and to resume full cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency on its nuclear programme. The joint declaration reaffirmed unwavering support for Ukraines sovereignty and territorial integrity, calling for a full, comprehensive and reciprocal ceasefire, and expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and Yemen over continued Houthi attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure. The statement also stressed that European countries must be included in negotiations on the continents future security.
stories.implication: Coordinated G7 condemnation of Hormuz disruption and demands for IAEA transparency increase the probability of further sanctions and naval presence decisions that will shape freedom-of-navigation operations and insurance risk calculus for regional operators.

stories.headline: US Navy seeks Super Intelligence concepts for new attack sub
stories.context: The US Naval Sea Systems Command has issued an open presolicitation closing November 13 seeking industry concepts for the use of what it calls Super Intelligence to help design its new attack submarine. The notice indicates the Navy plans to use an Other Transaction Authority mechanism in the coming stage of the effort, with an approach intended to reduce technical risk before procuring the first platform. Key requirements, schedule details and the precise extent of artificial intelligence use remain unanswered in the published notice.
stories.implication: NASEAs formal presolicitation for AI-assisted submarine design signals that autonomous design tools are entering the requirements phase of a major capital ship programme, which could reshape the competitive landscape for defence-focused AI engineering platforms.

stories.headline: Leonardo targets autonomous ASW missions for Proteus
stories.context: Leonardo is integrating Shield AIs Hivemind software into the digital twin of its Proteus uncrewed helicopter demonstrator at Yeovil in the UK, with the goal of enabling fully autonomous anti-submarine warfare missions for the UK Royal Navy. An agreement between Leonardo and Shield AI was announced at the end of October 2026 and is intended to expand Leonardos ability to build its own mission autonomy software for the rotorcraft platform. The ultimate goal described by Leonardo is making Proteus a dominant anti-submarine warfare platform.
stories.implication: If Hivemind enables a credible autonomous ASW capability on Proteus, it accelerates the Royal Navys path to a hybrid crewed and uncrewed carrier air wing and validates the software-first autonomy model for high-risk undersea warfare roles.

stories.headline: North East MPs push Lockheed for 2.4 billion Skynet 6 deal
stories.context: North East MPs have urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to award the 2.4 billion pound Skynet 6 military satellite communications contract to Lockheed Martin, which has linked the deal to a planned factory at NETPark in Sedgefield, County Durham, promising 500 direct jobs. The contract is disputed between Lockheed Martin and Airbus, with the Unite union warning that awarding it to the US firm would be a hammer blow to the British space industry and would create military dependence on the goodwill of the US President. Burnham told MPs he was completely committed to reindustrialisation and determined that the contract would drive good jobs in the region, though he said no final decision had been taken.
stories.implication: The Skynet 6 decision will set a precedent for whether the UK prioritises domestic industrial base continuity or allied industrial partnership on sovereign military communications infrastructure, with direct consequences for future satcom procurement strategy.

stories.headline: Warhound raises 200 million dollars to rebuild military dog supply
stories.context: Warhound, a startup co-founded by Colossal Biosciences founder Ben Lamm and Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey, raised 200 million dollars with the goal of rebuilding the domestic supply of dogs for the US military, law enforcement and first responders through cloning and gene editing. The company, which also includes former Palantir executive David Spirk as chief executive, plans to clone top-performing dogs, edit genes associated with health problems and introduce standardized training to puppies as young as two weeks old. Warhound estimates that around 80 percent of military working dogs are currently sourced from overseas and that more than half of dogs procured are ultimately deemed unfit for service.
stories.implication: A $200 million seed commitment for a biotech-defence hybrid targeting a documented military supply gap signals that non-traditional investors see government demand for biotechnology-enhanced operational assets as a fundable category alongside autonomous systems.
